evaluation.human_evals: The developer notes that comprehensive human evaluation is optimal but difficult to scale and reproduce, so they instead used LLM judges on MT-Bench and Alpaca-Eval, reporting average MT-Bench scores with standard deviation across three seeded runs. They also mention that users of their web service and app preferred most responses from the new chat models.
evaluation.results_summary: The developer reports an average score of 57.05 across six benchmarks for Qwen1.5-4B-Chat, with individual scores of 54.94 on Coursera, 47.00 on GSM, 57.92 on QuALITY, 69.15 on TOEFL, and 56.25 on SFiction.

identity.name: Qwen1.5-4B-Chat
identity.summary: Qwen1.5 is a series of open-source base and chat models released in multiple sizes, including a 4B chat variant.

possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: The card reports benchmark scores on factuality/quality tasks (GSM, QuALITY, TOEFL) and uses LLM judges instead of human evaluation, but does not report any hallucination or factual-grounding evaluation, so an open-weight chat model may produce factually inaccurate content.

specifications.model_size: 7.4 GiB of safetensors weights (7,900,793,992 bytes) in BF16
